name: connect-dashboard
description: Bare /connect on a device with no network opens the private code form titled Connect with 'network none' above the code field; /connect code opens the code-only Connect screen and says so in plain words when no code can be created; neither shows a 64-hex key (issue #121, Story 1).

config.command: bash -lc 'R=$(pwd); H="${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/kollab-spec-connect-dashboard"; mkdir -p "$H"; mkdir -p "$H/.kollab"; printf "%s" "{\"kollabor\":{\"llm\":{\"active_profile\":\"openai-test\",\"profiles\":{\"openai-test\":{\"provider\":\"openai\",\"model\":\"gpt-5.5\",\"base_url\":\"https://api.openai.com/v1\",\"api_key\":\"sk-test-dummy\",\"supports_tools\":true}}}},\"plugins\":{\"hub\":{\"enabled\":true}}}" > "$H/.kollab/config.json"; ln -sfn "$R/plugins" "$H/plugins"; cd "$H"; HOME="$H" PYTHONPATH="$R" "$R/.venv/bin/python" "$R/main.py" --no-daemon'

steps.title: no network: bare /connect opens the code form

steps.description: network none sits above the code field
the first device is told how to start a network
the code-only screen is titled Connect code
no network: the missing code is explained in plain words
no error text leaks into the screen
